mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) directly reduces the discount rate applied to equity cash flows, leading to higher equity valuations and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The rank correlation between FEDFUNDS and 20-day forward returns is less than 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A lower unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates a tightening labor market that supports corporate profit growth, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The rank correlation between UNRATE and 20-day forward returns is less than 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in housing starts (HOUST) below 1500.0 thousand units signals a weakening housing market, which is a leading indicator of economic contraction, driving negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The rank correlation between HOUST (below 1500) and 5-day forward returns is less than 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in industrial production (INDPRO) above 115.0 index points signals accelerating economic activity, which is a leading indicator of inflationary pressure, driving negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The rank correlation between INDPRO (above 115) and 60-day forward returns is less than 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 5.0% and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) is above 200.0, the market perceives a high-inflation environment that triggers a shift to defensive equity sectors, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The rank correlation between the interaction condition (FEDFUNDS>5.0 AND CPIAUCSL>200.0) and 20-day forward returns is less than 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When employment growth (PAYEMS) is negative and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is above 4.0%, the labor market is weakening, which signals a potential economic slowdown, driving negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The rank correlation between the interaction condition (PAYEMS growth rate < 0% AND UNRATE > 4.0%) and 5-day forward returns is less than 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime (defined by GDPC1 growth rate below 2.0% annualized for two consecutive quarters), the S&P 500 is vulnerable to profit margin compression, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 growth rate < 2.0% (annualized) for 2 consecutive quarters
failure_condition: The rank correlation between the regime condition (GDPC1 growth rate < 2.0% annualized for two consecutive quarters) and 60-day forward returns is less than 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a high inflation regime (defined by CPIAUCSL above 205.0 and FEDFUNDS above 5.0%), the Federal Reserve is likely to tighten monetary policy, which increases the discount rate and reduces equity valuations, driving negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The rank correlation between the regime condition (CPIAUCSL>205.0 AND FEDFUNDS>5.0%) and 20-day forward returns is less than 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
